slides.title: What is the purpose and who is the intended audience for the playbook?

paragraphs.text: What is the purpose and who is the intended audience for the playbook?

The purpose of this playbook is to provide comprehensive standards for creating 1–3-minute* technical videos for the Learn platform**. The playbook outlines the end-to-end process, with clear guidance on each step of creating a video.

The intended audience for this playbook is technical content developers in the Learning Lab team as well as other WWL teams involved in video production and publishing (i.e. Worldwide Learning Studios, Learning Product, LEO Engineering, and PDETs.)

*Median Watched Time of videos in the Microsoft Learn platform as per the C+ E Skilling Video Dashboard: Power BI
**These videos are also being leveraged in the Microsoft Learn Microlearning playlist in YouTube: Microsoft Learn - YouTube

PDETS: Product Development Engineering & Tool Services

slides.title: Instructional Design Principles for Educational Videos

paragraphs.text: Instructional Design Principles for Educational Videos
Use terminology the learners know (or explain it when introduced)
Explain why the topic matters and how it solves the learner’s problem
State what learners will learn or be able to do
All content in the video should support these objectives
Segment Content to Manage Cognitive Load
Chunk content into bite-sized segments or steps
Use clear transitions or sections for each subtopic or task

slides.notes: *See slides on Richard Mayer’s Principles of Multimedia Design for the full 12 multimedia principles

slides.title: Instructional Design Principles for Educational Videos

paragraphs.text: Instructional Design Principles for Educational Videos
Important information conveyed visually must be communicated via audio or text
Find ways to make learners engage mentally (i.e. ask a reflective question)
Embed a quick quiz or clickable interaction if the platform allows it
Give the correct answer and explanation in clickable interactive videos
Collect learner feedback to improve future iterations

slides.title: Richard Mayer’s Principles of Multimedia Design

paragraphs.text: Richard Mayer’s Principles of Multimedia Design
Humans learn best when extraneous, distracting material is not included
Humans learn best when they are shown exactly what to pay attention to on the screen
Humans learn best with narration and graphics, as opposed to narration, graphics, and text
Humans learn best when relevant text and visuals are physically close together
Humans learn best when corresponding words and visuals are presented together, instead of in consecutive order
Humans learn best when information is presented in segments, rather than one long continuous stream

slides.notes: How to Use Mayer’s 12 Principles of Multimedia Learning [Examples Included] - Water Bear Learning

slides.title: Richard Mayer’s Principles of Multimedia Design

paragraphs.text: Richard Mayer’s Principles of Multimedia Design
Humans learn more efficiently if they already know some of the basics
Humans learn best from visuals and spoken words than from visuals and printed words
Humans learn best from words and pictures than just words alone
Humans learn best from a more informal, conversational voice than an overly formal voice
Humans learn best from a human voice than a computer voice

Humans do not necessarily learn better from a talking head video. (If there is important information to be learned, relevant visuals on the screen will be more effective than showing a talking head of an instructor.)

slides.notes: How to Use Mayer’s 12 Principles of Multimedia Learning [Examples Included] - Water Bear Learning

slides.title: Video Prioritization Criteria

paragraphs.text: Video prioritization should be based on two major principles:
Alignment with strategic goals, such as supporting new product/feature launches, key marketing campaigns and Microsoft Solution Plays in that FY.
Data-driven decisions tied to WWL OKRs, including skilling 100M+ learners and 50M+ AI learners.
Video prioritization should leverage existing WWL tools and processes to minimize disruptions and avoid adding extra steps to the video creation workflow.

slides.notes:
Videos that have pre-aligned production timelines with WWL Studios/ Content Dev etc. should be given higher priority for production within those scheduled dates. 
(For instance, if a VTD video is slated for February 2026 and has been approved by WWL Studios, it should be prioritized for production accordingly)
